findings.text: The opening three paragraphs tell a newcomer what Athena is, what a study is, and that this page is Athena's study of firstmate. Someone arriving cold can say what the page is within seconds.
findings.source: header lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository."

findings.text: The page states why it matters: it shows Athena's reading ability. The citation links to pinned source lines back this up, because each claim links to a specific file and line range at the pinned commit.
findings.source: header lede: "Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project and explain it with every statement traced to a claim, and every claim to lines in the project's own files."

findings.text: The next step is visible at the top and linked to a section with two GitHub links. However, the page gives no install command, so a newcomer has to leave the page to learn how to try Athena.
findings.source: header: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself" and Next steps section

findings.text: These are Athena's selling points, but nothing on the page shows them. The page has no models, no checking step and no costs, so a newcomer who came for Athena sees only one sentence about it and a long study of a different tool.
findings.source: header lede: "has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost"

findings.text: The page promises that "agent" never means a worker. It then uses "old agent" and "running agent" for the worker being relaunched, which contradicts its own definition and confuses the reader.
findings.source: "Firstmate's own deciding AI, called the agent on this page and never a worker" vs. "If a relaunch fails after the old agent was stopped" (When things go wrong) and c18 "replaces the running agent with a new one"

findings.text: Several terms are used but never defined, even in the Glossary: "captain call", "endpoint", "durable record", and "pin" in the secondmate sense. A newcomer to firstmate cannot fully follow the failure and relaunch paths.
findings.source: Start here / t9 card: "still an open captain call"; t8: "recorded endpoint", "prior durable record", "re-reads its pin"

findings.text: Some definitions depend on terms that come later: "secondmate" in the early word list, and transition ids in Counters before the Transitions section. A first-time reader runs into these terms before they are explained.
findings.source: Words used first: "home ... A secondmate is a persistent home of its own"; Counters: "changed by transitions t1, t3, t4, t9, t11"

findings.text: The finding ids skip f2 with no explanation, which makes a careful reader wonder if something was left out. The limits are otherwise stated honestly, for example "none was run".

The page is careful to say what its sources do not support, for example the lack of retry bounds and of a captain deadline. This builds trust, but the many hedges make the main flow slow to read for a newcomer.
findings.source: "In scope ... The cited instruction does not say what makes work in scope, so this page gives no test for it."
